1

Item master

Every week: load the new item master exactly as downloaded from Dynamics, then send it to all stores. Each store laptop takes it by itself.

2

Passwords

Set each store's password, and HQ's. What you type becomes the password, and it is not shown again. A store's laptops take a new password within ten minutes.

3

Health check

Is every laptop reporting, sending, up to date and free of errors? Each laptop sends a short note every 15 minutes while it is open. The same check is emailed to you each morning.

4

Time on the app

Per store: how long was spent on each screen, and what was done. HQ's own time is shown on its own.

Sort a delivery

At the table: scan each piece once and put it on the pile the screen names. Then take the piles round: scan each bin's label, and put in what the screen lists.

Load today's sales
The Dynamics sales export, exactly as downloaded (.xlsx). One file can hold every store; this laptop takes only its own. Receipts already loaded are skipped, so an overlapping file is safe.
Deliveries
Load the transfer orders
The Dynamics “Transfer Order History” report for this store, exactly as downloaded (.xlsx) — do not open and edit it first. Designs in orders still Created are given bins: a bin already holding the design if it has room, otherwise a bin of the same category with room. Kits count as their pieces (KIT-5 = 5). A suggestion only — stock is still put away by scanning the bin.
Set up this store — load your bins and products, print labels, export what you recorded
1  Store code
The three letters from the Dynamics store code — EMP for S2004EMP. It goes on the shop floor, dock and write-off labels; bin labels carry the bin's own code (GF1-R01-S01-B01).
The full Dynamics store number. It picks this store's rows out of a sales file.
2  Bins — load the store's bin list
The Excel file (.xlsx, or .csv), one row per bin: stockroom, rack, shelf, bin, category, capacity (units it holds). Rack, shelf and bin can be written R01 or 1. Each bin's code is built from them: GF1-R01-S01-B01. Or one bin code column with that code. Replaces the bins below — for the first time, or to correct them; it warns first if a bin that holds stock would go.
2b  Or lay out racks as a block
A block is racks of one category: every rack gets the shelves, every shelf the bins, every bin the capacity. Codes run GF1-R01-S01-B01, GF1-R01-S01-B02 … Each block adds to the list; racks that differ are another block. A shelf holds one category.
No bins yet.
3  Products
The products come from HQ: the item master is loaded and sent to all stores in the HQ admin view, and this laptop takes it by itself. The Dynamics item master (“Item - bar code” export, .xlsx), exactly as downloaded — about a minute to read. It gives every product its bar code, name, size, category, design (search name) and, for kits, how many pieces they hold. Or a CSV with columns barcode, sku, description, category, size.
4  Labels
Stick one on each bin. Nothing can be scanned until they are up.
4b  Sales → refill list
Never refilled from a bin: items starting with these (bags, boxes).
Sales files are loaded from the Refill list on the main screen, so the store can load them without setup.
5  Get your data back
Opens straight in Excel. Export before you clear anything.
6  Sending to the server
Every movement, count and unrecognised scan is kept on this laptop and sent to the Google Sheet when there is a connection. Scanning never waits for it. Setting it up: server/SETUP.md.
